newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India extends run, nervous Taiwan slips.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India extends run, nervous Taiwan slips.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts tracked local shares higher on Thursday as continued fund buying in Bombay aided sentiment, traders said.
But Taiwanese GDRs were softer after the country's central bank tightened monetary policy in a surprise move which analysts there said was likely to lead to a fall in the stock market.
Taiwanese stocks rallied to close above the key 10,000 level on Thursday before the interest rate changes.
In India, investors showed little concern for some weak first quarter earnings reports, with key GDRs extending recent gains. Hindalco added 37 cents to $36.50/37.50 and SBI added $1 to $27.50/28.50.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.86 points firmer at 87.91, a 2.16 percent rise, with the premium over the local market at 23.11 percent from 21.27 percent.
The Cazenove Indian GDR index added 1.01 points to 97.23 -- a 20.45 percent premium to the local market. It measures from midday on the previous trading day to midday today.
Bombay's benchmark index rose 60.87 points to 4,305.76.
Taiwanese GDRs were mostly softer, Advanced semiconductors shedding 90 cents to $24.85/$25.85 from earlier highs over a dollar better.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index shed 2.86 points, or 2.02 percent, to 139.05, representing a discount to the local market of 3.84 percent.
Taiwan's weighted index added 1.24 percent on the day to 10,066.35.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index shed 0.49 points to 73.05 points, a premium of 44.89 percent over the local market.
